scope.note: ACA 15 proposes adding Section 5 to Article XXI of the California Constitution, which would bar a Member of the Legislature who voted for ACA 8 from being a candidate for congressional office in a district adopted under subdivision (b) of Section 4, the provision ACA 8 adds. Section 5 would become operative only if ACA 8 is approved by the voters and takes effect and that subdivision becomes operative. ACA 15 itself would also need to be adopted by both houses and approved by the voters. Whether these conditions were met is not recorded in this dataset.

scope.note: Pennsylvania's deadline for receiving mail-in ballots in the 2020 general election. In the sentences left out of the passage, the dissent says that the Pennsylvania Democratic Party sued in state court and argued that the court could extend the deadline under the clause of the State Constitution providing that elections shall be “free and equal” (art. I, § 5); that is the argument the state court agreed with.

support.document: the Court's order denying review, issued with opinions dissenting from the denial; the passage is from Justice Thomas's dissent
support.quote: in October 2019, the Pennsylvania Legislature overhauled its election laws. […] The Pennsylvania Supreme Court agreed. On September 17, it held that this “free and equal” provision enabled the court to extend the deadline three days to accommodate concerns about postal delays.
